note: Chronological fields (zadok_year_born/died, gregorian_year_born/died, lifespan_years) are GENERATED, not hand-edited here -- see references/build/genealogy_chronology.py and docs/data/genealogy/generated/. This file holds only the raw per-tradition textual facts (traditions) and their citations; the generator walks the chain from Adam (year 0) forward per timeline_variant defined in index.json.

people.name: Adam
people.title: First Man, Father of All

name_study.textual_basis: Genesis 2:7 makes the connection explicit: formed 'of dust from the ground' (adamah).

discrepancies.description: LXX adds 100 years to age-at-Seth's-birth versus MT/SP (which agree at 130), subtracting the same from years-after -- total lifespan (930) is identical in all three traditions.

people.name_meaning: Man, mankind; from 'adamah' (ground) -- Genesis 2:7 makes the connection explicit (formed from the dust of the ground)

people.name: Eve
people.title: First Woman, Mother of All
people.note: Not part of the Genesis 5 age-tracked chronology chain -- no traditions data (Genesis gives no lifespan formula for Eve); zadok_year_born is a fixed pin at Creation, not generated.

major_events.description: Deceived by serpent, ate forbidden fruit (Genesis 3:1-6)

people.name_meaning: Life; she gives life (mother of all living)

people.name: Cain
people.title: First Son, First Murderer
people.note: Not part of the Genesis 5 age-tracked chronology chain -- no traditions data; zadok_year_born is a fixed pin, not generated. Child 'enoch_cain' (Genesis 4:17) is not yet a record in this dataset.

major_events.description: Marked by God, banished east of Eden (Genesis 4:15)

people.name: Abel
people.title: First Shepherd, First Martyr
people.note: Not part of the Genesis 5 age-tracked chronology chain -- no traditions data; zadok_year_born/died are fixed pins, not generated. Died young/childless, no lifespan data given in the text.

major_events.description: Brought firstlings of flock; accepted by God (Genesis 4:4)

people.name_meaning: Breath, vapor, emptiness; transience of life

people.name: Seth
people.title: Third Son, Appointed Heir

name_study.textual_basis: Genesis 4:25 gives the wordplay explicitly: 'God has appointed (shat) for me another offspring instead of Abel.' Not a reconstructed etymology -- the narrator states it.

discrepancies.description: Same +100/-100 pattern as Adam; total lifespan (912) identical across all three.

people.name_meaning: Appointed, set; from 'shith' (to put, appoint) -- Genesis 4:25 states the wordplay itself ('God has appointed me another offspring')

people.name: Enosh
people.title: Son of Seth

name_study.textual_basis: Common-noun meaning is well attested (distinct from adam/generic-mankind and ish/individual-man); used for human frailty against God's greatness, e.g. Psalm 8:4, 103:15. No in-text narrator wordplay the way Seth/Noah get -- inferred from usage elsewhere in the OT, not an explicit gloss.

discrepancies.description: Same +100/-100 pattern; total lifespan (905) identical across all three.

people.name_meaning: Mortal man, frail man; a term for humanity distinct from 'adam'/'ish', emphasizing frailty against God's greatness (e.g. Psalm 8:4) -- inferred from usage elsewhere, not an in-text gloss

people.name: Cainan
people.title: Son of Enosh

name_study.gloss: uncertain -- no TWOT root for the name itself

root.meaning: possibly related to קִינָה (H7015, 'lament, elegy') via the shared ק-י-נ core, but Kenan's own final consonant differs (ן vs ה) -- not a confirmed derivation

name_study.textual_basis: Popular chains gloss this 'sorrow', but that rests on an unconfirmed root link, not an attested one. Do not assert it as settled.

discrepancies.description: Same +100/-100 pattern; total lifespan (910) identical across all three.

people.name_meaning: Meaning uncertain -- no TWOT root exists for the name itself; the popular gloss 'sorrow' rests on an unconfirmed link to a different root and should not be treated as settled

people.name: Mahalalel
people.title: Son of Enosh -- distinct from the LXX-only Cainan of Genesis 11, see cainan_gen11

name_study.textual_basis: Transparent theophoric compound: mahalal ('praise', from halal) + el ('God') -- same name-formation pattern as Daniel, Immanuel. Not in dispute.

discrepancies.description: Same +100/-100 pattern; total lifespan (895) identical across all three.

people.name_meaning: Praise of God; theophoric compound of 'halal' (to praise) and 'El' (God)

people.name: Jared
people.title: Son of Mahalalel

name_study.textual_basis: Direct nominal form of the verb 'to descend'. Popular chains' 'shall come down' gloss is accurate to the root.

discrepancies.description: MT and LXX agree exactly here (162/800/962) -- Jared is the one antediluvian patriarch where LXX does NOT apply its usual +100 shift.

SP shortens both the age-at-heir-birth (62 vs 162) and the total lifespan (847 vs 962) -- not merely a redistribution, a genuinely shorter total. Matches published SP comparison tables (this is not a digitization artifact in this repo's source text).
discrepancies.theological_significance: Part of a broader SP pattern (see Methuselah, Lamech below) of shortening the antediluvian era relative to MT/LXX -- worth asking whether this is a deliberate SP compression or whether MT/LXX independently lengthened. Not resolved here.

people.name_meaning: Descent; direct nominal form of 'yarad' (to come down, descend)

people.name: Enoch
people.title: Son of Jared, Walked with God

name_study.textual_basis: Same root as Proverbs 22:6's 'train up a child'. Popular chains gloss this 'teaching', which is a loose paraphrase -- 'dedicated/initiated' is closer to the actual root.

discrepancies.description: Same +100/-100 pattern; total (365) identical across all three -- notably matching the days in a solar year, a coincidence often remarked on but not textually explained.
discrepancies.theological_significance: Enoch is 'not found, because God took him' (Gen 5:24) -- the only antediluvian patriarch with no death notice, read since antiquity (and in Hebrews 11:5) as a type/foretaste of bodily translation without death.

people.name_meaning: Dedicated, initiated; from 'chanak' (to train up, dedicate) -- same root as Proverbs 22:6; the popular gloss 'teaching' is a loose paraphrase

people.name: Methuselah
people.title: Son of Enoch, Longest-Lived Man

component_2.alt: שֶׁלַח (H7973, twot 2394a, 'missile, dart, javelin', same root family)

name_study.textual_basis: Two real readings, not one solid and one invented: (1) plain/onomastic -- 'man of the javelin' (mtei + shelah-as-weapon), a warrior name with no eschatological content; (2) homiletical -- 'his death shall bring/send [it]' (mut + shalach-as-verb), read as a sentence-name. Reading (2) gains real force from the numbers: under BOTH MT's and LXX's own total-lifespan figures (969 in both), his death year lines up with the Flood year -- see discrepancy note below. This needs the fuller diachronic/synchronic word-study-method.md treatment before the study draft leans on either reading with confidence.

discrepancies.description: MT (187+782) and LXX (167+802) both total 969 -- the longest human lifespan recorded in any tradition -- via different splits.

On a strict reading of LXX's own numbers for Methuselah, Lamech, and Noah, Methuselah would still be alive more than a decade after the Flood begins -- a long-noted internal problem with the LXX figures as transmitted, not a claim this study is making up.
discrepancies.theological_significance: If the name really does mean 'his death shall bring [judgment]', a post-Flood survival directly undercuts the name's own force -- one reason some see this as evidence of scribal corruption specifically in LXX's Methuselah/Lamech numbers, distinct from the systematic (and internally consistent) +100 pattern seen elsewhere in LXX Genesis 5.

discrepancies.description: SP shortens Methuselah's total from 969 to 720 (67+653) -- a genuinely different total, not a redistribution. This is widely read as a deliberate correction so Methuselah dies in the very year of the Flood, avoiding the LXX post-Flood-survival problem above.
discrepancies.theological_significance: If Methuselah's name does carry the 'his death shall send [the Flood]' sense, SP's number is the one tradition where the name and the math actually agree without needing any further harmonization.

people.name_meaning: Genuinely ambiguous between two real readings -- 'man of the javelin' (m'tei + shelach) or 'his death shall send [it]' (mut + shalach) -- both parse correctly and nothing in the lexicon settles which was intended

people.name: Lamech
people.title: Son of Methuselah, Father of Noah

name_study.gloss: unknown -- no TWOT root exists for this name
name_study.textual_basis: Popular chains gloss this 'despairing' or 'powerful man' -- neither is lexically demonstrated from Hebrew. Standard lexicons mark the derivation genuinely uncertain (possibly a non-Hebrew Semitic loanword). Do not force a gloss in the study draft.

discrepancies.description: Unlike most Gen 5 patriarchs, all three traditions give genuinely different totals: MT 777, LXX 753, SP 653 -- not a clean redistribution pattern.
discrepancies.theological_significance: MT's 777 is often noted as a deliberate numerological contrast with the 'human number' 666 elsewhere in Scripture (Revelation 13:18) and with the murderous Lamech of Genesis 4:23-24's '77-fold' vengeance boast -- worth treating as a real feature of MT specifically, not assumed present in LXX/SP's different numbers.

people.name_meaning: Meaning unknown; no TWOT root exists and standard lexicons mark the derivation genuinely uncertain

people.name: Noah
people.title: Son of Lamech, Ark Builder

name_study.textual_basis: Genesis 5:29 explicitly glosses the name via paronomasia (sound-play) on nacham ('this one shall comfort us'), NOT a strict derivation from nuach ('rest', H5117, twot 1323) despite Noah's name sounding closer to the latter. Popular chains that flatten this to simply 'rest' are collapsing a real, deliberate double wordplay into one word.

discrepancies.description: Genesis 5:32 gives Noah's age at fathering Shem/Ham/Japheth as a flat 500 (used here for age_at_heir_birth); Genesis 7:11 puts the Flood at Noah's 600th year; Genesis 11:10 says Shem was 100 'two years after the Flood', which implies Shem was born nearer Noah's 502nd year, not exactly his 500th. This ~2-year wrinkle (likely because the three sons weren't triplets and Shem wasn't necessarily born the moment Noah turned 500) is a known minor internal tension, not a textual-tradition variant -- flagged rather than silently smoothed over by adjusting the number.

people.name_meaning: Genesis 5:29's own wordplay is with 'nacham' (to comfort), not 'nuach' (rest), despite the similar sound -- a real double sound-play, not a simple derivation
